CLOSED RECORD (tan-cli#269). `crates/` is deleted; the binary described below
cannot be rebuilt from this repository, the modules named in the recipe are
gone, and TAN_PARITY_LIVE / TAN_PARITY_CAPTURE no longer exist. Nothing here
is a runnable instruction any more -- the recipe and the two machine-read
lines are kept VERBATIM because they are the record of how these answers were
obtained and which `crates/` tree produced them. Read this file; do not try to
follow it, and do not hand-edit a recorded value to make something pass. The
store moved from `tests/parity/oracle_fixtures/` to
`tests/fixtures/oracle_captures/` in the same change; every path below is
written as it stood at capture time.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------

Every *.json fixture in this directory was captured from an actual run of the
Rust oracle -- never inferred from crates/ or a docstring (docs/ROADMAP.md's
Standing Rules) -- via:

  cargo build --bin tan
  TAN_PARITY_LIVE=1 TAN_PARITY_CAPTURE=1 TAN_RUST_BINARY=<path to the built
    tan(.exe)> python -m pytest tests/parity/test_oracle_parity.py \
    tests/parity/test_clean_parity.py tests/parity/test_flash_oracle_parity.py \
    tests/parity/test_image_size_oracle.py tests/parity/test_run_oracle_parity.py

oracle binary:  tan 0.4.1  (`tan --version`)
oracle source:  crates/ at 204c3a0b8dcb165e10ac3d14f3e9bfa699e45b59
                "fix: close five RC follow-ups -- flake, TBD sentinel, repr
                parity, CI coverage, prog name" -- the last commit that
                touched crates/ as of the capture, per `git log -1 -- crates/`.
                That SHA, not whichever commit HEAD happened to be at when
                `cargo build` ran, is what determines the binary's behaviour
                and what a future re-capture must diff against.

                Both lines below are MACHINE-READ, by
                tests/parity/test_oracle_provenance.py -- do not reword them
                without changing that test (tan-cli#409). The claim they
                encode used to be prose only, and it had silently gone stale
                by three commits; see the drift section at the end of this
                file.

captured-from-crates-commit: 204c3a0b8dcb165e10ac3d14f3e9bfa699e45b59
verified-against-crates-commit: c0e45f955c2f4b3d40e9193dcb89b7ca1d3a5f76
worktree HEAD:  b40109b46aefdd42d82ff30f89c8bf8d5061d72d (unrelated python/
                commits on top; does not affect the oracle binary)
captured:       2026-08-01 (tan-cli#272)
platform:       Windows (win32) -- a case gated `WINDOWS_CASES` in
                test_clean_parity.py was captured on a host where that gate
                is true; re-capturing on a non-Windows host will leave those
                keys untouched (the test itself still skips there) rather
                than overwrite them with something else.

See tests/parity/oracle_fixtures.py's own module docstring for the replay
mechanics (TAN_PARITY_LIVE / TAN_PARITY_CAPTURE, the PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST-
keyed store, and why a missing key is a loud KeyError rather than a skip).

Re-capturing: this file used to say "crates/ is frozen and will not change
again for this reason, so there should be no reason to re-run the capture
recipe above". That was false when it was written and nothing checked it --
see the drift section at the end. What holds is the weaker, checkable claim:
re-run the capture recipe above when crates/ MOVES past
`verified-against-crates-commit`, or when a NEW case is added to one of the
five files it lists (a new argv, a new tree
shape). Capturing is additive -- `oracle_fixtures.resolve()` only ever adds
or overwrites the keys the run you did touch, so a partial capture (e.g.
`pytest tests/parity/test_flash_oracle_parity.py -k some_new_case`) is safe
and does not disturb any other module's fixture file.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------

test_oracle_parity.json's `test_generate_matches_rust_with_a_resolvable_sdk`
case -- one exception to "no reason to re-run unless a new case is added"
above -- was captured separately, 2026-08-01, once a clean alp-sdk checkout
existed to capture it against (it was skipped at the original freeze: the
only reachable checkout then was dirty and mid-flight, and capturing against
that would have frozen bad provenance):

  cargo build --bin tan
  ALP_SDK_PARITY_ROOT=<clean alp-sdk checkout, pinned at the ref below> \
    TAN_PARITY_LIVE=1 TAN_PARITY_CAPTURE=1 TAN_RUST_BINARY=<built tan(.exe)> \
    python -m pytest tests/parity/test_oracle_parity.py \
    -k test_generate_matches_rust_with_a_resolvable_sdk

oracle binary:  tan 0.4.1 (unchanged -- crates/ is still frozen at
                204c3a0b, above; only this one case was missing a fixture)
alp-sdk ref:    v0.15.0-rc1 (996937ac4b452260628cf2c6adad4be31483a3d4) --
                the SAME ref as HAND_PORT_PINNED_SDK_COMMIT
                (python/tests/gates/test_planner_relocation_freshness.py)
                and PINNED_SDK_TAG (.github/workflows/parity.yml), by
                construction: that agreement is why this ref and not
                another.

This ONE case is bound to alp-sdk CONTENT, not just the frozen Rust binary --
unlike every other fixture in this store. `tan generate` reads the SDK's
metadata/emit-registry to decide which of the 9 default targets render and
whether each succeeds (`data.written`/`data.failed`), so a checkout with
different metadata could legitimately produce a different frozen answer.
`sdk.root` (the one field that would otherwise embed the capture host's own
checkout path) is scrubbed on both sides via the same `oracle_fixtures.scrub`
mechanism `work`/`home` already use, so the frozen fixture replays on any
host with any equivalently-pinned checkout at any path -- but "equivalently
pinned" is the part a future reader must not assume forever. If
PINNED_SDK_TAG in .github/workflows/parity.yml ever moves past v0.15.0-rc1,
re-capture THIS ONE CASE against a clean checkout at the new pin (the recipe
above, run against that checkout) rather than trusting the old answer still
holds -- nothing else in this store depends on alp-sdk content, so nothing
else needs re-capturing for a pin bump alone.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------

2026-08-01, same day, second pass: ten keys in test_oracle_parity.json were
re-captured after `tests/gates/test_no_leaked_host_paths.py` -- and,
separately, a maintainer reading the pushed commit -- caught real host paths
sitting in this file's own committed JSON, unscrubbed:

* `test_validate_board_yaml_missing_guard_matches_the_oracle_at_exit_2`,
  `test_validate_no_sdk_guard_is_a_known_divergence_from_the_oracle`,
  `test_sdk_switch_unresolvable_version_is_a_known_divergence_from_the_oracle`
  (3 keys): each called `rust_run(..., scrub_roots=())` on the reasoning that
  its own assertions only read a small literal exit code / issue code -- true,
  but irrelevant, because `oracle_fixtures.resolve()` still persists the WHOLE
  captured envelope regardless of what the test looks at, and each envelope's
  `project.root`/`data.boardYamlPath`/the refusal `message` carried the
  capture host's own `work_dir`/`home` verbatim. Fixed by widening each call
  to `scrub_roots=(work_dir, home)` -- scrubbing costs nothing here, since the
  assertions never inspected those fields either way.
* `test_plan_from_shows_the_plan_and_writes_nothing` (all 6 parametrised
  cases) and `test_plan_from_with_materialise_writes_every_artefact` (7 keys):
  a DIFFERENT, THIRD root -- neither `work_dir` nor `home` -- leaked here.
  These tests copy a real committed plan fixture
  (`tests/parity/oracle/*.build-plan.json`, repo root, the Rust-workspace
  tree -- outside this file's own ownership) into the scratch dir and run
  `build --plan-from` against it unmodified; a bare `--plan-from` relays the
  plan unsubstituted (`generate_cmd.py`'s own docstring on why Rust's
  `--plan`/`--plan-from` substitute nothing), so every slice's
  `env.ALP_SDK_ROOT` -- and `m55_hp`'s `appDir` -- carried the ACTUAL
  filesystem path of whichever alp-sdk checkout those six plan fixtures were
  themselves captured against, verbatim, into this file. Fixed by adding
  `oracle.compare()`'s `extra_scrub_roots` parameter (empty by default, so
  every other caller is unaffected) and having each of these two tests read
  the leaking root straight off the copied plan file's own
  `slices[*].env.ALP_SDK_ROOT` before calling `compare()`, so the scrub
  target is derived from the fixture rather than hardcoded to one capture
  host's path.

Neither fix, on its own, touched `tests/parity/oracle/*.build-plan.json`
itself (repo root, a different tree) -- only the copy that had landed HERE,
in this file. That source WAS a separate, real leak of its own (a
colleague's macOS checkout path, `8e1838a`/PR #5, 65 occurrences across the
six plan files -- a DIFFERENT person's machine than the three pytest-tmp-path
leaks above), closed in the same pass once found: see
`tests/parity/oracle/`'s own git log for that fix (the six plan files'
`env.ALP_SDK_ROOT`/`appDir`/sysbuild-arg fields, replaced with the generic
`/srv/alp-sdk` placeholder). `test_no_leaked_host_paths.py`'s LEAKS table was
widened in the same change (a bare `/Users/<name>`, no drive letter -- the
shape that leak took, and the shape the gate had never checked) since it
demonstrably did not catch that leak either; see that file's own git log.
Re-capturing the 7 plan-derived keys against the fixed plan files changed
NOTHING in this JSON -- the dynamic scrub (`_embedded_sdk_root`) already
normalizes whatever root a plan embeds to the same `<ORACLE-ROOT-N>` token
regardless of its value, so this file was already correct either way.

Also added: `oracle_fixtures._refuse_if_leaking_a_real_host_path`, called
from `resolve()`'s CAPTURE branch, refuses to persist any future capture
whose envelope still carries a `C:\Users\<name>`, `/home/<name>` or
`/Users/<name>`-shaped absolute path (scanning the same JSON-escaped text
this module is about to write, so a doubled-backslash Windows path cannot
slip past it the way it did `test_no_leaked_host_paths.py`'s single-
backslash pattern once already). Unit-tested in `test_oracle_fixtures.py`.
That gate only sees TRACKED files and so cannot catch a leak until well
after `git add`; this one runs at the moment of capture instead.

Re-capture recipe for the 10 affected keys (unchanged binary/SHA/ref from
the sections above -- this was a scrubbing bug in the test harness, not a
change in what the oracle answers):

  cargo build --bin tan
  ALP_SDK_PARITY_ROOT=<clean alp-sdk checkout at v0.15.0-rc1> \
    TAN_PARITY_LIVE=1 TAN_PARITY_CAPTURE=1 TAN_RUST_BINARY=<built tan(.exe)> \
    python -m pytest tests/parity/test_oracle_parity.py \
    -k "test_validate_board_yaml_missing_guard_matches_the_oracle_at_exit_2 \
        or test_validate_no_sdk_guard_is_a_known_divergence_from_the_oracle \
        or test_sdk_switch_unresolvable_version_is_a_known_divergence_from_the_oracle \
        or test_plan_from_shows_the_plan_and_writes_nothing \
        or test_plan_from_with_materialise_writes_every_artefact"

Verified after this pass: `grep -rn "Users" python/tests/parity/oracle_fixtures/`
returns nothing, `tests/gates/test_no_leaked_host_paths.py` passes with every
file in this directory (and this file's own new `test_oracle_fixtures.py`)
tracked, and the other four fixture files in this directory are byte-
identical to before this pass (`git diff --stat` on each is empty).

path stub `validate.spawn-not-implemented` -- the divergence the old test name
recorded is gone, and the test was renamed with it. Keys here are pytest node
ids (`oracle_fixtures._current_key`), so the rename moves the key; the stored
ORACLE answer under it is byte-identical and was NOT re-captured (nothing
about the Rust binary changed). The re-capture recipe in the 2026-08-01 pass
above still names the OLD spelling, deliberately -- it is a record of what was

THE CAPTURE HOST'S TOOL INVENTORY IS PART OF THE FROZEN ANSWER
(tan-cli#313, tan-cli#324)

Seven cases branch on a `which()` probe, so their frozen answers encode which
tools the CAPTURE host had -- not just what the oracle computes. The capture
host had:

  west       ABSENT   -- the three west_forward cases froze the
                         "west not found on PATH" launch error
  dd         PRESENT  -- the yocto_wic cases froze "would run dd if=..."
  bmaptool   ABSENT   -- else those cases would have frozen a bmaptool argv

Replay pins the PYTHON side's PATH to match that inventory, so the comparison
does not silently measure the replay host instead of the port. The pins:

  test_flash_oracle_parity.py  `_TOOL_PROBE_PINNED_CASES` (4 cases) ->
    `_pin_tool_inventory`, a scratch PATH holding a stand-in `dd` only
  test_oracle_parity.py  `test_west_forward_matches_rust[migrate|lock|quality]`
    (3 cases) -> `oracle.empty_tool_inventory`, a scratch PATH holding nothing

CONSEQUENCE FOR RE-CAPTURE, and the reason this section exists: the recipe at
the top of this file NO LONGER WORKS AS WRITTEN for these seven. Under
TAN_PARITY_LIVE=1 both sides genuinely spawn, so `compare()` REFUSES a
`python_env_overrides` rather than compare one pinned side against one
unpinned side -- deliberately, since that would be a fresh divergence rather
than a capture. Measured:

  TAN_PARITY_LIVE=1 python -m pytest \
    "tests/parity/test_oracle_parity.py::test_west_forward_matches_rust"
  -> 3 failed, RuntimeError: compare() got python_env_overrides under
     TAN_PARITY_LIVE=1

To re-capture any of the seven, run the capture on a host whose tool
inventory MATCHES the table above (no `west`, no `bmaptool`, a real `dd`) and
drop the pin for that run. Capturing on a host with `west` installed and the
pin dropped would freeze a different answer entirely -- one that then only
replays on hosts that also have `west`, reintroducing exactly the bug
tan-cli#324 closed.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------

THE FROZEN-crates/ CLAIM WENT STALE, AND NOTHING NOTICED (tan-cli#409)

This file used to state, as the reason no re-capture could be needed, that
"crates/ is frozen and will not change again for this reason". By the time
that was read again, crates/ had moved four commits past the recorded capture
SHA -- three of them real `src/` changes, i.e. changes that CAN change the
binary these fixtures were captured from:

  8a71310  docs: align the repository with the Python port (#386)
             crates/tan-cli/README.md, crates/tan-core/README.md -- docs only
  ac79d4c  feat: close the v0.6 issue wave (#352)
             crates/tan-cli/src/commands/debug_config.rs (4654 lines),
             crates/tan-cli/src/commands/build/preflight.rs
  4b7d2c4  fix(test): guard doctor's westResolved fixture (#333) (#340)
             crates/tan-cli/src/commands/bootstrap/steps.rs,
             crates/tan-cli/src/commands/doctor.rs
  909ba02  fix(test): route ensure_venv through exit_code_shim (#318)
             crates/tan-cli/src/commands/bootstrap/steps.rs

The recorded SHA appeared nowhere but in this file's own prose, so nothing
could compare it against anything. It is machine-read now
(`verified-against-crates-commit`, checked by
tests/parity/test_oracle_provenance.py, which FAILS when
`git log <that sha>..HEAD -- crates` is non-empty), and the same drift can no
longer go quiet.

Why `verified-against-crates-commit` was advanced to 8a71310 with NO
re-capture. Measured on this tree, darwin, both runs minutes apart over the
five modules the capture recipe at the top of this file names:

  frozen replay (port vs these fixtures)
    3 failed, 222 passed, 13 skipped, 4 xfailed
  TAN_PARITY_LIVE=1 (port vs an oracle built from THIS checkout, tan 0.4.1)
    8 failed, 219 passed, 11 skipped, 4 xfailed

Every case that ran in BOTH modes passed in both. Port == fixture and
port == current binary over the same cases means fixture == current binary on
every surface those cases compare -- including
`test_debug_config_resolution_matches_rust` and
`test_debug_config_native_host_preview_global_format_matches_rust`, which are
the two frozen cases ac79d4c's 4654-line `debug_config.rs` rewrite could have
moved and did not.

What that measurement does NOT cover, stated so nobody reads it as more than
it is:

  * the eight tool-probe-pinned cases (the section above). They are the
    live run's 8 failures, every one of them the documented
    `compare() got python_env_overrides under TAN_PARITY_LIVE=1` refusal --
    structurally unable to run live, so unable to be cross-checked this way.
  * anything win32-gated. This was run on darwin, where those cells skip in
    BOTH modes; the platform line above still governs.
  * the one alp-sdk-CONTENT-bound case, which needs ALP_SDK_PARITY_ROOT at
    v0.15.0-rc1 and skipped here.
  * the fifteen cases that have no fixture at all -- see PARITY-COVERAGE.txt
    in this directory, which is where that hole is now recorded.

A capture, not a re-verification, is still what a change to a compared
surface demands. This one earns its SHA bump by measurement, not by the
assertion that crates/ cannot move.

2026-08-04: THIS STORE IS NO LONGER SINGLE-PLATFORM (tan-cli#409)

Fifteen new keys were captured on darwin, not on the `platform:` line's
win32. They close part of the live-only hole PARITY-COVERAGE.txt records --
three cases that used to spawn the oracle behind `skipif(RUST is None, ...)`
and would have become passing SKIPS the day tan-cli#269 deletes crates/, plus
twelve first-ever comparisons for verbs nothing compared at all:

  test_build_sdk_root_oracle_parity.json   1 key   (was live-only)
  test_run_oracle_parity.json              2 keys  (were live-only)
  test_command_surface_oracle_parity.json  12 keys (new module: completion,
                                                    trace, scaffold, inspect,
                                                    bootstrap, kconfig,
                                                    examples)

  cargo build --bin tan
  TAN_PARITY_LIVE=1 TAN_PARITY_CAPTURE=1 python -m pytest \
    tests/parity/test_build_sdk_root_oracle_parity.py \
    tests/parity/test_run_oracle_parity.py \
    tests/parity/test_command_surface_oracle_parity.py

oracle binary:  tan 0.4.1, target/debug/tan built from THIS checkout --
                certified by oracle_provenance.drift() against
                PINNED_ORACLE_BUILD_INPUT_DIGEST, which is the check that
                makes "built from the pinned crates/ state" a measurement
                rather than a claim (tan-cli#414).
oracle source:  crates/ at 8a71310, i.e. unchanged from
                verified-against-crates-commit above.
platform:       darwin (macOS 26.5.2)

The four pre-existing `test_run_oracle_parity.json` help-text keys were NOT
re-captured. A capture run rewrites every key the run touches, and this one
did rewrite them -- `Usage: tan.exe run` became `Usage: tan run`, the prog
name being the one thing in that text the capture PLATFORM decides. They were
restored to their win32 originals afterwards, so those four keep the
provenance this file records for them. Nothing else in this directory
changed.

Why capturing these on darwin is safe, key by key -- the question the
`platform:` line exists to force. A frozen answer is only a valid oracle for
a replay whose separator style matches, so each of the fifteen was checked
for host-shaped content before it was committed:

  * fourteen carry no filesystem path at all beyond a bare `<ORACLE-ROOT-N>`
    token (`project.root`), or no path whatsoever (the completion scripts,
    the empty `data` skeletons). A bare token has no separator in it, so
    there is nothing for a platform to render differently.
  * the fifteenth, `test_inspect_matches_the_oracle`, carries
    `<ORACLE-ROOT-0>/board.yaml`. That case -- and only that case -- forces
    `oracle_fixtures.normalise_scrubbed_path_separators(..., force=True)` on
    BOTH sides. The automatic rule keys off CAPTURE_PLATFORM and so disables
    itself on win32, which is right for the win32-captured majority and
    exactly backwards for a POSIX-captured key: without the override, a
    Windows replay would diff this fixture's `/` against its own live port's
    `\` and report a platform difference as a port defect.

What could NOT be captured here, and must be captured on win32 by whoever
takes it on: the two `test_support_bundle_oracle_parity.py` cases. They are
not merely separator-sensitive -- their whole compared surface (doctor's
check list and statuses, the whole inspect.context) is decided by the host,
and no scrub reaches that. Measured on this machine, the oracle's own bundle
under `empty_tool_inventory` froze these rows, among others:

  codeLLDBExtension  unknown  vadimcn.vscode-lldb: unknown ...
  lldb               pass     vadimcn.vscode-lldb ships its own LLDB ...
  zephyrSdkAvailableForHost   pass  The Zephyr SDK publishes a host build
                                    for macos-aarch64.

`macos-aarch64` is this host's architecture written into the frozen answer,
and the two LLDB rows are the macOS debug stack; a Windows bundle carries
`longPaths` (which exists nowhere else) and no LLDB rows at all. Freezing
this on darwin and replaying it against a live port on any other OS diffs two
platforms' genuinely different -- and both correct -- behaviour, which is the
false red `CAPTURE_PLATFORM` exists to warn about. Note what does NOT save
it: `_refuse_if_leaking_a_real_host_path` does not fire on this capture (a
scratch destination under the system temp root carries no `/Users/<name>`
shape), so the guard would have written it. The reason to refuse is the
platform, and it has to be a decision, not a hope that the leak guard
notices.

that measurement could have caught moving.

2026-08-04, second darwin capture: the last live-only cases in
test_oracle_parity.py (tan-cli#409)

Nine new keys, again on darwin rather than the `platform:` line's win32.
Seven tests (nine node ids -- `test_explain_matches_the_oracle` is
parametrised three ways) that used to spawn the oracle behind
`@_ORACLE_REQUIRED`, i.e. gated on binary PRESENCE with no fixture behind
them. Every one would have become a passing SKIP the day tan-cli#269 deletes
crates/, with the run still exiting 0. The decorator itself is gone: this
module now has no binary-presence skip left except its own two harness
self-tests.

  test_oracle_parity.json   9 keys   (were live-only)

    test_explain_matches_the_oracle[overview|unknown-template|unknown-target]
    test_renode_no_sdk_matches_the_oracle
    test_size_missing_manifest_is_a_known_divergence_from_the_oracle
    test_run_no_sdk_is_a_known_divergence_from_the_oracle
    test_model_bare_invocation_is_a_known_divergence_from_the_oracle
    test_monitor_is_a_known_divergence_from_the_oracle
    test_faultdecode_is_a_known_divergence_from_the_oracle

  cargo build --bin tan
  TAN_PARITY_LIVE=1 TAN_PARITY_CAPTURE=1 \
    TAN_RUST_BINARY=target/debug/tan python -m pytest \
    tests/parity/test_oracle_parity.py -k "<the seven names above>"

oracle binary:  tan 0.4.1, target/debug/tan built from THIS checkout --
                certified by oracle_provenance.drift() against
                PINNED_ORACLE_BUILD_INPUT_DIGEST.
oracle source:  crates/ at 8a71310, i.e. unchanged from
                verified-against-crates-commit above.
tree:           f3208e1
platform:       darwin (macOS 26.5.2)

The `-k` selection is not cosmetic. A capture run REWRITES every key it
touches, so running the whole module would have re-captured the 42
pre-existing keys on darwin and silently replaced their provenance -- the
same hazard the note above records for test_run_oracle_parity.json's four
help-text keys, where the restore had to be done by hand afterwards.
Selecting the seven names avoided it rather than repairing it. Verified by
diffing the store before and after:

  keys 42 -> 51,  ADDED 9,  CHANGED 0,  REMOVED 0

Why capturing these on darwin is safe. Four go through
`test_oracle_parity._both_sides`, which scrubs work_dir/home out of BOTH
sides and then applies `normalise_scrubbed_path_separators(..., force=True)`
to both -- `force` because the automatic rule keys off CAPTURE_PLATFORM and
so disables itself on win32, which is exactly backwards for a POSIX-captured
key. The other three (`model`, `monitor`, `faultdecode`) assert only a
`command` string, an exit code and an issue code, so they take
`rust_run(..., scrub_roots=())` -- the spelling
`test_new_som_matches_the_oracle_on_command_and_issue_code` already uses.

One case needed more than the shared helper, and it is worth naming:

  test_size_missing_manifest_is_a_known_divergence_from_the_oracle

pins the oracle's `io::Error` Display verbatim, and that string is
PLATFORM-dependent -- POSIX reports ENOENT (2) "No such file or directory"
where Windows distinguishes a missing DIRECTORY and reports
ERROR_PATH_NOT_FOUND (3) "The system cannot find the path specified." The
test branched on `os.name == "nt"`. Under a frozen replay that is now wrong:
the string is decided by the CAPTURE host, so a Windows replay reads back the
darwin tail and the `os.name` branch would redden it against a perfectly good
fixture. The condition is now `os.name == "nt" and oracle_fixtures.LIVE` --
the replay host decides only when the oracle is really being spawned.

Measured on this tree with target/ moved aside, i.e. exactly the state
tan-cli#269 produces:

  with the binary present:  335 passed,  97 skipped, 13 xfailed
  no target/ at all:        293 passed, 148 skipped,  4 xfailed

`test_oracle_parity.py` contributes ZERO oracle-presence skips to that 148
now. What remains, counted from the same run, is declared in
`test_parity_freeze_completeness.py` and is NOT this capture's to close:

   2  test_support_bundle_oracle_parity.py  -- needs a win32 host (see the
                                               section above for why no scrub
                                               reaches `macos-aarch64` or a
                                               Windows-only `longPaths` row)
  47  test_scaffold_content_oracle_parity.py -- compares a FILE TREE, which
                                               no fixture store in this
                                               package can hold yet

--------------------------------------------------------------------------

2026-08-04, third darwin capture: the scaffold TREES (tan-cli#409)

A second store, `scaffold_trees.json`, and a second reader,
`tests/parity/scaffold_fixtures.py`. Not keys in the file above, because what
is frozen here is not an envelope: `test_scaffold_content_oracle_parity.py`
diffs a whole scaffolded FILE TREE, and it does so from two tests sharing one
memoised spawn per template -- so a key derived from `PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST`
would have depended on which of the two ran first. Keyed by TEMPLATE ID
instead.

  scaffold_trees.json   6 templates, 40 files, 120522 bytes

    board-diagnostics  6 files      minimal-app      8 files
    edge-ai-starter    8 files      sensor-starter   6 files
    iot-starter        6 files      zephyr-app       6 files

  cargo build --bin tan
  TAN_PARITY_LIVE=1 TAN_PARITY_CAPTURE=1 \
    TAN_RUST_BINARY=target/debug/tan python -m pytest \
    tests/parity/test_scaffold_content_oracle_parity.py

oracle binary:  tan 0.4.1, target/debug/tan built from THIS checkout.
oracle source:  crates/ at 8a71310, unchanged from
                verified-against-crates-commit above.
platform:       darwin (macOS 26.5.2)

Stored as TEXT, not base64, and that is a measurement rather than a
convenience. All six templates at DEFAULT_SOM_SKU (E1M-AEN801) were checked
before the store was designed: 40 files, EVERY ONE valid UTF-8, and NOT ONE
containing the scratch directory it was scaffolded into. So there is nothing
to scrub -- unlike every key in the envelope store -- and nothing to encode,
and a committed fixture whose values are the actual CMake/YAML/Markdown text
is reviewable in a diff. `scaffold_fixtures._as_text` FAILS the capture on a
non-UTF-8 byte sequence rather than laundering it through
`errors="replace"`, so if a template ever vendors a binary asset the capture
stops and the decision gets revisited.

Newlines survive: json round-trips LF and CRLF distinctly and the reader does
no translation, so a CRLF-vs-LF divergence between the two binaries still
fails the comparison -- `_read_tree`'s own docstring reads raw bytes
precisely so nothing launders a real divergence, and this store does not undo
that.

Measured with target/ moved aside, i.e. exactly the state tan-cli#269
produces:

  with the binary present:  335 passed,  97 skipped, 13 xfailed
  no target/ at all:        331 passed, 101 skipped, 13 xfailed

The gap is FOUR tests, and all four are declared by name in
`test_parity_freeze_completeness.py`: the two harness self-tests, which take
the binary as their SUBJECT and can never be frozen, and the two
`test_support_bundle_oracle_parity.py` cases, which need a win32 host for the
reason the earlier section gives in full. `_UNFROZEN` is now EMPTY.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------

2026-08-04, the PLATFORM-BOUND store: captured on three CI runners
(tan-cli#409)

A third store, `platform_bound.json`, read by
`tests/parity/platform_fixtures.py`. Keyed `<case>::<sys.platform>`, because
what `test_support_bundle_oracle_parity.py`'s two cases compare -- doctor's
whole check list and statuses plus the whole `inspect.context` -- is decided
by the HOST as much as by the binary. One frozen answer cannot serve three
platforms, and the store NEVER falls back to another platform's key.

  platform_bound.json   6 keys

    failing-host::darwin   failing-host::linux   failing-host::win32
    resolved-sdk::darwin   resolved-sdk::linux   resolved-sdk::win32

Captured by `.github/workflows/capture-platform-fixtures.yml`, run
30913698426, all three jobs `success`:

    capture (ubuntu-latest)   -> linux
    capture (windows-latest)  -> win32
    capture (macos-latest)    -> darwin

platform:       NOT one host. Each key was captured on the runner whose
                `sys.platform` it names. This is the first store in this
                directory for which the `platform:` line above is a
                per-key fact rather than a file-wide one.

The recorded blocker for these two was "needs a win32 host, and nobody has
one". That was half right: a single-keyed store genuinely cannot hold them,
but the win32 machine was never missing -- this repository runs
`windows-latest` on every PR. What was missing was a job that captured on it.

TWO THINGS MEASURED WHILE COLLECTING, both worth keeping:

1. `resolved-sdk::darwin` from `macos-latest` DIFFERS from the same key
   captured on this developer's own darwin box, in exactly one field:

       .doctor.checks[4].detail   "lldb" (runner)  vs  "lldb-dap" (local)

   Check NAMES and STATUSES are identical, and `_statuses` -- what
   `_assert_doctor_sections_match` compares -- reads only `(name, status)`.
   So the difference is inert for every assertion, and the CI-captured key
   replays green on a local box whose `lldb` resolves differently. Verified
   by replacing the local capture with the runner's and re-running with
   `target/` moved aside. Recorded because a future reader diffing this
   store against their own capture WILL see it and should not read it as
   drift.

2. Merging the three artifacts was ORDER-DEPENDENT, and silently wrong. A
   runner starts from the committed store, so `platform-bound-ubuntu-latest`
   also carried the `darwin` keys that were already committed -- and
   `sorted()` put it after `platform-bound-macos-latest`, so a stale
   `darwin` key overwrote the fresh one `macos-latest` had just captured.
   Caught by diffing the two darwin captures before merging, NOT by a test.
   Fixed on both sides: the workflow now filters to its own `sys.platform`
   before uploading, and `platform_fixtures.merge_from` REFUSES a
   multi-platform artifact outright rather than silently picking one.

Measured with target/ moved aside, i.e. exactly the state tan-cli#269
produces:

  tests/parity, no target/ at all:  336 passed, ZERO oracle-presence skips

`_UNFROZEN` and `_PLATFORM_BOUND` are both EMPTY. Every case in this package
now replays without a Rust binary except the two harness self-tests, which
take the binary as their SUBJECT and never could.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------

2026-08-07, PR #511 fix round: TWO KEYS RENAMED, NOTHING RE-CAPTURED, one
prior round wrongly changed the VALUES on the same rename and this pass
restores them.

  test_flash_matches_the_rust_oracle[multi-segment-interface-is-allowed]#0
    -> test_openocd_program_word_diverges_from_the_oracle_by_exactly_the_brace[multi-segment-interface-is-allowed]#0

  test_flash_matches_the_rust_oracle[openocd-forced-bin-appends-base]#0
    -> test_openocd_program_word_diverges_from_the_oracle_by_exactly_the_brace[openocd-forced-bin-appends-base]#0

Moving these two cases out of the byte-diff CASES table in
test_flash_oracle_parity.py was the maintainer-authorised fix for the
unconditional-brace change to `openocd_program_word` -- they are documented,
by-exactly-one-brace divergences from the oracle now, not exact matches, so
they needed a dedicated test rather than a slot in the byte-diff table. That
move is correct and stays. What the same commit ALSO did, wrongly, was
change the recorded VALUES under the new keys: `buildRoot` and the two
`message` strings went from the oracle's actual win32-native
`<ORACLE-ROOT-0>\.\build` form to a POSIX-shaped `<ORACLE-ROOT-0>/./build`
that the win32 CAPTURE never produced. `oracle_fixtures.py`'s own
`CAPTURE_PLATFORM = "win32"` and `normalise_scrubbed_path_separators` short-
circuits on the capture platform (`REPLAY_IS_CAPTURE_PLATFORM`) -- so on
Windows nothing reconciles a doctored `/` fixture against live `\` output,
and the two cases failed there. Restored both values to their byte-identical
e402952 form (`<ORACLE-ROOT-0>\.\build`, `...\build\a.elf`,
`...\build\a.bin`); verified by matching every case in this store by NAME
(not key) against e402952 -- 54 cases, 56 total entries on both sides,
zero value diffs once these two were restored.
